question.text: Same quantity of ice is filled in each of the two metal containers $P$ and $Q$ having the same size, shape and wall thickness but made of different materials. The containers are kept in identical surroundings. The ice in $P$ melts completely in time $t_{1}$ whereas in $Q$ takes a time $t_{2}$. The ratio of thermal conductivities of the materials of $P$ and $Q$ is

solution.text:
We know that Relation between temperature gradient (TG) and thermal conductivity $(K)$
So,
$$
\frac{d \theta}{d t}=-K A \frac{d \theta}{d x}=-K A \times(\mathrm{TG})
$$
Le. $\mathrm{TG} \propto \frac{1}{K}\left(\frac{d \theta}{d t}=\right.$ constant $)$
or $K \times \frac{1}{T}$
$$
\begin{array}{l}
K_{1} \times \frac{1}{t_{1}} \\
K_{2} \times \frac{1}{t_{2}}
\end{array}
$$
From the Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$$
\frac{K_{1}}{K_{2}}=\frac{1 / t_{1}}{1 / t_{2}}
$$
$$
K_{1}: K_{2}=t_{2}: t_{1}
$$
